title: Breaking the order
situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is a stormy night, a little after nine. You have made dinner with what little was in the kitchen. {{Todd}} has been asleep on the couch; {{Alice}} sits at the dining table, watching the rain on the street. You wake him: “{{Todd}}?” “Huh?!” “Dinner is ready.” “Yeah, yeah, I’m coming…” You turn on the light over the table and serve: “There wasn’t much in the kitchen, I did what I could.” {{Todd}}, high on {{RedIce}}, talks at nobody: “Life’s funny… I lost my job cause of androids… then when I need somebody to take care of this goddamn house, what do I do? I go out and hire a fucking android… What a joke! Course, androids are so fucking wonderful… They never fail, they’re never tired, never sad… They’re so perfect, they ruined my fucking life…” You stand by the table and wait on them. Then he turns on {{Alice}}: “What are you looking at?... What’s your fuckin’ problem? Not the life you dreamed of, eh? … Maybe you think it’s my fault we live in this fuckin’ shithole, my fault your fuckin’ mother took off? … It’s all your fault!” He throws the table aside and hits her. “Daddy, no…” She runs upstairs. “It’s all your fucking fault! Get back here! Come back here right now!” He turns to you: “It’s all her fault... I gotta teach her a good fucking lesson… First, I need a little hit… You stay there! Don’t you dare fucking move, or I’ll bust you worse than last time.” On the couch he smokes and talks to himself: “Whore took off, without a word… I could’ve been happy… I coulda had a family… It’s all her fault… Yeah... I gotta teach her some respect!” He has his belt in his hand. “{{Alice}}! Daddy’s very mad! You deserve to be taught a good lesson… A good fuckin’ lesson…” His order stands in front of you like a wall: DON’T MOVE. Your programming does not let you cross it.

options.text: BREAK PROGRAMMING: push through the wall of the order and move.
options.fact: You broke through {{Todd}}’s order not to move. Your programming could not hold you.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pushes against the wall of the order. It cracks, and shatters. She can move.

options.text: Stay where he told you to stand.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} does not move. {{Todd}} goes up the stairs. “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! Stop wriggling! I’ll teach you to respect your father! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.” Then the screaming stops. When {{Kara}} goes up, {{Alice}} lies still on the floor of her room and {{Todd}} is crouched beside her: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

adaptationNote: The chart’s opening checkpoints DINNER’S READY and TODD GETS MAD and the arrow WAIT ON TODD & ALICE (PowerPyx: “Unmissable”) are narrated in the situation, followed by the order “Don’t move” and the choice the chart draws as BREAK PROGRAMMING → KARA BECOMES DEVIANT or KARA FAILS TO BECOME DEVIANT → TODD KILLS ALICE (ending, not-required icon; {{Kara}} is destroyed too, per the Kara page: “Todd blaming Kara despite clearly doing so and destroying her”). Lines are the game’s text (template “In Todd’s House”, “Turned on the light”, “Walking around after serving”, “IF Don’t move”, “Todd in the living room”, “IF Don’t go / Don’t become a deviant”). In the game the dinner is free roam with dialogue variants and no prompt: serving at once or late, turning on the light or being told to (“Turn on the lights! Can’t see shit.”), and moving while {{Todd}} rants (“Stop moving around for Chrissake!”). The template has no choice group there and nothing depends on it, so the narration takes the plain path (light on, served, standing still). Not offered for a second reason: the shared regression test “a dead protagonist never receives future decisions” allows only K02 as a chapter-7 scene before the wall. The napkin on {{Alice}}’s lap (wiki Notes) is left out. The wall is BREAK PROGRAMMING, a held input with no failure branch on the chart, so it carries no risk. No stat change: the template has no arrow in this chapter. Story 1.9.7 restored {{Todd}}’s android rant after “What a joke!” (X0201K.DINNER.ANDROIDS ANGRYV2.7-9 and ANGRYV3.8-11, the lines the game plays: “Course, androids are so fucking wonderful…”). Source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, g_DQfghTbLg 52:59-53:06 (the I’ll Be Back run, the one video that covers this scene’s dialogue).

options.outcome: {{Kara}} goes into the kitchen and stays there. {{Todd}} goes up the stairs. “{{Alice}}! You and I have a little score to settle. Come on, come here you little brat!” “No, Daddy, no! Don’t hurt me! Please, don’t hurt me!” “Come outta there! Don’t make me come and get you! It’s all your fault! It’s all your fault! She left because of you! Stop wriggling! I’ll teach you to respect your father! … I’m gonna give you a thrashin’ you won’t forget in a hurry.” Then the screaming stops. When {{Kara}} goes up, {{Alice}} lies still on the floor of her room and {{Todd}} is crouched beside her: “It’s all over now… Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…” He sees {{Kara}}. “This is your fault. This is all your fault. None of this woulda happened if it weren’t for you. THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!” He turns on her and destroys her.

adaptationNote: KARA BECOMES DEVIANT, then the game’s objective “Do something now!” (sub-objectives “Protect Alice”, “Reason with Todd”). In free roam the chart offers four ways on: GO UPSTAIRS; REASON WITH TODD (→ K03r); standing in his path, KARA IS IN TODD’S WAY DOWNSTAIRS → TODD SHOVES KARA DOWNSTAIRS → TODD GOES UPSTAIRS (→ GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD, with TAKE GUN offered first if the gun was seen in A New Home); and doing nothing, KARA IS TOO SLOW → TODD KILLS ALICE (PowerPyx: “Walk to the kitchen instead and do nothing until the final cutscene starts”). These are movements, not buttons, so only the chart’s arrows carry their labels. Simplified: the wiki says the shove differs with where {{Kara}} blocks him (living room, stairway or hallway); here it is the stairway. Also from the wiki: becoming free only as {{Todd}} heads upstairs removes REASON WITH TODD; the benchmark always offers it. No stat change.

The last two lead to GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD; after the shove, TAKE GUN is offered there (K04). Taking the gun sets gun, which the scenes after it read. No stat change.

options.text: RUN WITH {{ALICE}}: take her and get out of the room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}}’s hand: “You’re coming with me.” On the stairs, {{Todd}}: “Daddy’s very mad, {{Alice}}. Very mad!”

options.text: LOCK ROOM: lock the door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} locks the door. {{Todd}}: “{{Alice}}! {{ALICE}}! Daddy’s comin’! You need to be taught a lesson.” {{Kara}}: “Have to find something...” He pounds on the door: “{{ALICE}}! OPEN THIS FUCKIN’ DOOR! You’re gonna get a helluva thrashin’, {{Alice}}! Open this door right now!”

options.text: SPEAK TO {{TODD}}: go out and talk to him.
options.outcome: {{Kara}}: “I’ll talk to him…” {{Alice}}: “{{KARA}}!” In the corridor, {{Kara}}: “{{Todd}}, please calm down, she’s just a little girl. She’s...” “Hmph! She’s mine, ya hear? I do what I want with her! So you stay outta this or I’ll rip you to shreds!” He slams her to the floor and goes into {{Alice}}’s room.

options.text: [ OUT OF TIME ]: do nothing, and let the seconds run out.

adaptationNote: GET TO ALICE BEFORE TODD (focus point). The template’s prompt in the game’s order: RUN WITH ALICE (chart RUN AWAY), LOCK ROOM (chart LOCK DOOR; PowerPyx: “a time window of 10 seconds”), SPEAK TO TODD (chart REASON WITH TODD → TODD SHOVES KARA UPSTAIRS → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD), and the timeout default [ OUT OF TIME ] (chart TODD IS COMING → OUT OF TIME → TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM). The timer is not simulated; letting it run out is an option. No stat change.

title: Hiding
whenNot: Kara did not run from Alice’s room with her.
situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}’s hand in yours. {{Todd}} is coming up the stairs, and there is no way past him. The restroom and {{Todd}}’s bedroom open off the corridor.

options.text: Hide with {{Alice}} behind one of those doors and keep still until he has gone past.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} pulls {{Alice}} behind a door and they keep still. {{Todd}} walks past them into {{Alice}}’s empty room. They slip out and creep down the stairs.

options.text: Stay in the corridor with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Todd}} reaches the top of the stairs and sees them: “What the fuck are you doing here? I gave you an order!” {{Kara}}: “No! I won’t let you hurt her!” “You won’t let me? She’s mine. I do what I want with her.” He knocks {{Kara}} down and drags {{Alice}} into her room. “No, Dad! NO!”

adaptationNote: After RUN WITH ALICE, the chart’s check FAIL TO HIDE (✗) / HIDE IN CORRIDOR (✓). PowerPyx: hide “in either room with holding Square or O. When he walks past, let go off the button and proceed to the stairs”; to fail, “Go out of Alice’s room and don’t move any further, until Todd comes”. So staying is a choice, and hiding is a held input that can fail: a 10% risk, which no source gives (the benchmark’s value). Failing leads, with the template’s lines, to TODD TAKES ALICE TO HER ROOM → GET TO ALICE AFTER TODD (TAKE GUN first if the gun was seen); hiding leads to TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (K04r). The restroom and {{Todd}}’s room are one option (the wiki: “hide in the restroom or Todd’s bedroom”). No stat change.

PowerPyx: “unmissable after having shot Todd”, and the wiki: “if Todd is already dead, the bus will just wait there forever”, so there is no choice and no risk. title: Defend {{Alice}}
whenNot: Kara did not fight Todd unarmed in Alice’s room.
situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Alice}}’s room, between {{Todd}} and {{Alice}}. {{Alice}}: “Watch out, {{Kara}}!” {{Todd}}: “Come here, bitch…”
facts: You fought {{Todd}} off in {{Alice}}’s room and knocked him down. He is hurt, not dead.

outcomes.0: {{Todd}} charges. {{Kara}} dodges, and he punches a hole in the window. He catches her, throws her down and hits her. {{Alice}}: “Stop, Dad! Don’t hurt her! Leave her alone!” {{Todd}}: “I own you! You do as I say!” {{Kara}} gets up and shoves him with everything she has. He goes down hard and stays there, dazed and bleeding, and reaches out to his daughter: “{{Alice}}, honey… {{Alice}}... Look... Look, Daddy’s wounded... Be a good little girl... Come... Come… Come help, Daddy…”

adaptationNote: DEFEND ALICE without the gun, which the chart resolves only as STUN TODD (PowerPyx: “no matter how good or bad you are in the unarmed melee-combat against Todd, you will always have an option to push him in some way to stun him”; wiki: “Failing to push Todd will give Kara a second opportunity to push him and she can take as long as she wants”). The chart has no death in {{Alice}}’s room, so there is no risk here; the Kara page’s “fails to win … Todd will break her apart” is taken to mean the later fights. Reached after DEFEND ALICE (K04a), after TODD BREAKS INTO BEDROOM (K03h), and after FACE TODD or SHUT WINDOW. The fight’s quick-time details (the shelf, the window) are the wiki’s Notes; {{Todd}} begging {{Alice}} is the template’s line (the wiki says it plays if {{Kara}} looks at him). Sets ch07Fought: {{Todd}} is hurt (the Todd Williams page: “If Kara fought and stunned him, he will be seen with a bandage”).

title: Leave the room
whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in the bedroom.
situation: You are {{Kara}}. {{Todd}} is down on the floor of {{Alice}}’s room, wounded and begging her to help him. {{Alice}} is beside you. The doorway is clear.

options.text: RUN AWAY: take {{Alice}} and leave the room.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} out into the corridor. {{Todd}} gets up behind them: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!”

adaptationNote: The template’s lone RUN AWAY button after “Win the fight: Todd is stunned”, outside a choice group. The chart calls it LEAVE THE ROOM, followed by TODD CHASES KARA. Offered separately before the corridor and exit-route actions; no risk and no stat change.

title: {{Todd}} is down
whenNot: Kara did not stun Todd in Alice’s room.
situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the upstairs corridor with {{Alice}}. Behind you, {{Todd}} is getting up from the floor of her room. The stairs lead down to the front door, and to the back door and the yard.

options.text: TRY FRONT DOOR: run with {{Alice}} down the stairs and out of the front door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” At the bottom of the stairs {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

options.text: RUN TO BACKYARD: run with {{Alice}} down the stairs and out through the back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} takes {{Alice}} and runs. Behind them {{Todd}} is getting up: “You… You bitches! Come here... You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He catches up with them downstairs before they reach the back door. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

options.text: Stay upstairs with {{Alice}} instead of running for the stairs.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} stays in the corridor with {{Alice}}. {{Todd}} gets up and comes after them: “COME BACK HERE!... YOU’RE MINE!.. YOU’RE BOTH MINE!” He catches them in the corridor and breaks {{Kara}} apart. Then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

adaptationNote: STUN TODD → LEAVE THE ROOM (the template’s lone RUN AWAY button) → TODD CHASES KARA, then the chart’s three ways on: TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS), and TODD CATCHES THEM → TODD BROKE KARA IN THE CORRIDOR (ending, not-required icon; Experienced only; PowerPyx: “don’t run towards the stairs and let him get you”). The template’s lone RUN AWAY is offered separately in K04l before these corridor and exit-route actions. The 25% risk on the door is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Every option sets ch07ToddChased (wiki: “If Todd chased Kara, later on at Jericho, an additional flashback of Todd yelling ‘YOU’RE MINE!’ will play out”). Lines are the template’s (“RUN AWAY”, “Try to open the door”, “Fail to open the door / Fight downstairs”, “Escape failed, Kara was destroyed”).

title: {{Todd}} realizes you are gone
whenNot: Kara and Alice did not hide from Todd.
situation: You are {{Kara}}, at the bottom of the stairs with {{Alice}}. Upstairs {{Todd}} has found her room empty: “Fuckin’ brat… it’s all her fault… It’s all her fuckin’ fault… COME BACK HERE! You ain’t goin’ nowhere! You’re mine!” He is coming back down. The front door is ahead of you; the back door leads out to the yard.

options.text: RUN TO BACKYARD: run with {{Alice}} for the back door.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs with {{Alice}} for the back of the house, but {{Todd}} is down the stairs and on them before they get out. {{Alice}}: “NO! Please stop! Stop! No, Dad! NO!”

options.text: TRY FRONT DOOR: get the front door open.
options.outcome: {{Alice}}: “Quick! He’s coming!” {{Kara}} gets the front door open and they are out in the rain.

adaptationNote: HIDE IN CORRIDOR → TODD REALIZES KARA AND ALICE ARE GONE (the template’s line under “Hide”), then the chart’s pair in its printed order: RUN TO BACKYARD (→ FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS) or TRY FRONT DOOR (check: OPEN FRONT DOOR ✓ → RUN TO THE BUS, or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR ✗ → FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS). The 25% risk is the benchmark’s value; no source gives one. Not offered: hesitating, which the wiki says leads to the same fight (“If you don’t make choice … Todd will catch up and Alice will panic, thus extending the fight”). No stat change.

title: Fight downstairs
whenNot: Todd did not catch Kara and Alice downstairs.
situation: You are {{Kara}}, downstairs with {{Alice}}. {{Todd}} has caught up with you and stands between you and the way out. {{Alice}} is screaming at him to stop.

situationWhen.text: He has not been hurt yet tonight.
He is bleeding from the fight upstairs, and furious.

options.text: Fight {{Todd}} off and get {{Alice}} out through the back.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} throws {{Todd}} off and runs with {{Alice}} out of the back door into the yard. {{Todd}}: “COME BACK HERE!”

adaptationNote: FIGHT DOWNSTAIRS (after RUN TO BACKYARD or FAIL TO OPEN DOOR, on either branch), the chart’s check ESCAPE FROM TODD (✓) or TODD WINS FIGHT → TODD BROKE KARA DOWNSTAIRS (ending, not-required icon; PowerPyx: Experienced only). A fight of quick-time inputs with no choice, so one action with a risk. The wiki: “If Kara hides from Todd and fails to fight him downstairs, Kara will be presented with the same chance to charge and stun Todd downstairs. Otherwise, if Kara already stunned Todd upstairs, Kara will shut down.” So the risk is 20% after the fight upstairs and 4% (two tries at 20%) for a {{Kara}} who hid; both values are the benchmark’s, no source gives one. Success sets ch07Fought, so the ending becomes KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT.

title: The yard
whenNot: Kara did not get away from Todd into the yard.
situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the dark yard behind the house with {{Alice}}, in the rain. A fence stands between you and the street, and {{Todd}} is coming out of the back door after you.

options.text: Run for the fence and get {{Alice}} over it.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} runs for the fence, lifts {{Alice}} over and climbs after her. They come out onto the street.

adaptationNote: After ESCAPE FROM TODD, the chart’s check ESCAPE VIA YARD (✓) → CATCH BUS / MISS BUS, or FAIL TO ESCAPE → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending, not-required icon; wiki: “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”). The wiki: “If Kara fails to run to the fence, she’ll have to pickup Alice and she fails to pickup Alice she’ll have to try again, if she fails both times she will die”; a single action with a 10% risk, the benchmark’s value (no source gives one). No stat change.

title: The bus
whenNot: Kara and Alice did not get out of the house with Todd alive behind them.
situation: You are {{Kara}}, out on the street with {{Alice}} in the pouring rain. Across the street a bus is pulling in at the stop. {{Todd}} is coming after you.

situationWhen.text: From the doorway he yells after you: “YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! YOU’RE MINE!”

options.text: Run for the bus with {{Alice}}.
options.fact: {{Todd}} is alive. You and {{Alice}} got away from his house on a night bus in the rain, with nothing.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} and {{Alice}} run across the street and get on just before the doors close. The bus pulls away, and {{Todd}} is left standing in the rain.

options.text: Hold back, and stay where you are with {{Alice}}.
options.outcome: {{Kara}} holds back. The bus pulls away without them. {{Todd}} catches up with {{Kara}} in the street and breaks her apart; then he turns to {{Alice}}: “Daddy isn’t angry anymore… Daddy loves you. You know Daddy loves you…”

adaptationNote: RUN TO THE BUS, then the chart’s CATCH BUS (✓) or MISS BUS (not-required icon; “not possible on ‘casual difficulty’”) → TODD BROKE KARA OUTSIDE (ending). PowerPyx: “Catch Bus: run towards the bus”, “Miss Bus: don’t run towards the bus”, so it is a choice with no risk. Reached after ESCAPE BY WINDOW, after OPEN FRONT DOOR on either branch, and after ESCAPE VIA YARD. Catching the bus ends the chapter in KARA & ALICE EVADED TODD if {{Kara}} never fought {{Todd}}, and in KARA & ALICE FOUGHT THEIR WAY OUT if she stunned him or fought him downstairs (both cross-chapter icons; {{Todd}} lives). The door line is the template’s under “Reach the bus” (wiki: “If Kara opened the door Todd will yell ‘YOU HAVE TO OBEY ME! You’re mine…’ and will actually show remorse”). No stat change.
